sections.heading: Choosing the Right Center Point for Faces
paragraphs: Portraits have natural focal points — the eyes and upper face — and centering the circular crop on that region produces a more engaging avatar than simply targeting the geometric middle of the photo.

For group shots or product photos, the subject may sit off-center, so adjusting the mask position is essential. A tool that lets you drag the crop interactively gives you visual feedback that static presets cannot.
Getting the center right means your round thumbnail communicates the same clarity as the full-size original, even at the tiny dimensions used in comment threads and messaging apps.

sections.heading: When Circular Crops Appear in Print
paragraphs: Corporate ID badges, conference name tags and membership cards frequently require round portrait photos. Providing a clean circle-cropped image to the print vendor saves them adjustment time and prevents awkward auto-cropping that cuts off the top of someone's head.

Event programs and yearbook layouts also benefit from uniform circular portraits that create a consistent visual rhythm across pages. Having all images pre-cropped to the same circle diameter keeps the layout tight and professional.
Exporting at a resolution appropriate for print rather than screen ensures the round image remains sharp on paper as well as on display.

sections.heading: Transparency Outside the Circle for Clean Compositing
paragraphs: Rather than a white square, the space outside the circle is transparent, enabling the round photo to sit on colored cards or dark themes without rectangles.
This is exactly what design teams expect for delivery to web and app projects.
If a solid background is needed instead, simply place the circle crop onto a colored canvas during output.

sections.heading: Social Media Avatar Sizes Across Platforms
paragraphs: Every major social platform crops profile images to its own circle or rounded shape, and the safest asset is a clean circle-cropped square that each platform can display without further distortion. Supplying a ready round image avoids the platform guessing where your face is.

Comment threads, story rings and call tiles all reuse the profile image at small sizes, so a centered circular crop keeps you identifiable in every context. Preparing one clean source prevents awkward crops in features that cannot be customized.
A near-identical circular crop also satisfies most app store listings and community badges, giving you a single image that works across the whole public identity surface.

sections.heading: Photo Quality and Resolution for Round Output
paragraphs: The quality of the round result depends on the source resolution, and exporting at a size that matches the destination avoids pixelation. Generating the circle crop at the exact pixel dimensions a profile field expects keeps the avatar crisp rather than scaled down later.

High-resolution sources also give you freedom to adjust the center point without the image becoming blurry. Starting from a well-lit, sharp portrait produces a round avatar that holds up on retina displays and large monitors alike.
When the same round image will serve print materials, exporting a larger version alongside the web size preserves flexibility for both uses.

A perfect round avatar is now always a minute away.

faqs.q: Can I reposition the circle on the image?
faqs.a: Yes. Drag the circular mask to center the subject exactly where you want, with live preview of the final round result.

faqs.q: Does the output have a transparent background?
faqs.a: Yes. Outside the circle is transparent, so the round image composites cleanly over any background or theme.

faqs.q: Is circle cropping free and private?
faqs.a: Yes. Processing happens entirely in your browser with no uploads, watermarks or accounts.

faqs.q: What image format should I use for the round output?
faqs.a: PNG is recommended because it preserves the transparent background outside the circle. JPEG does not support transparency and would fill the corners with a solid color.
